svg.text: B Shared front end — own-lid dosing at a tipper dock
Each storage box keeps its own dosing lid; the dock only turns, shakes and weighs it. Nothing shared touches the food before free fall.
source: B-process-line.md section 1.1
used by all four B concepts
dock: 0–180°, 15 Nm, 3 load cells, 150 Hz vibrator, 1 finger
The tipper dock
Clamp frame on a horizontal axis (15 Nm), on three load cells,
with a 150 Hz vibrator and one linear finger for the lid.
The dose is measured as loss in weight at the dock.
M mesh lid: flour, sugar, spices

g.text: no moving part in the food

svg.text: Stainless mesh (2–5 mm) over the whole opening. Cohesive powder
bridges and holds even upside down; it flows only while the
dock vibrates. ± 0.2 g (spice dock), ± 2 g (bulk).
I iris lid: rice, lentils, pasta, peas

g.text: top view: the finger turns the ring

svg.text: A silicone sleeve iris (as Mucon valves), 0–100 mm opening,
twisted open and shut by the dock finger; closes gently on
product without crushing. ± 1 piece, ± 3 g for rice.
O open lid: potatoes, onions, meat pieces
Pulse-tilt to 95–130° over a vibrating chute watched by a camera;
each pulse lets one piece go and the dock stops on weight.
Resolution: one piece.
S spout lid: oil, milk, stock, cream
A silicone duckbill spout doses by tilt angle with weight
feedback; tilted back, the duckbill closes drip-free.
± 2 g. Mains water goes in by valve and flow meter.
K piston box: mince, quark, butter
The box floor is a free piston. Upside down over the vessel,
the dock pushes it and a wire cuts off the extruded slug.
± 3 %; empties sticky contents almost completely.
Each panel loops by itself. Weak point: four lid types add cost and 20–30 mm of height per box; the mesh needs tuning per product class.
